sentence: This project studies how single cells inside endometrial cancers differ in their genes and gene activity, and how those tumors change over time.
This project tries to find out how obesity changes the proteins the intestine releases and how those proteins affect immune cells in fat tissue.
This project studies how two gene mutations work together to cause problems in making blood cells, using zebrafish and stem cells.
This project builds modern lab and computer methods that test chemical safety without animals and compares chemicals to judge their safety.
This project studies how pancreatic cancer cells invade veins, using three-dimensional imaging and gene activity measurements in human pancreatic cancer samples.
This project supports clinical trials and laboratory research on how drugs and other treatments work safely in children and in pregnancy.
This project improves imaging tools so doctors can better evaluate spinal disease in people with psoriatic arthritis and personalize treatment.
This project studies how mutant versions of a cancer gene change gene expression to drive cancer growth.
This project uses nanotechnology to engineer a pathway in dendritic cells so the immune system can fight cancer better.
This project uses computer software to analyze chest scans from lung cancer screening and find lung changes caused by chronic respiratory disease in Veterans.
This project uses computer design and chemical synthesis to make molecules that block a bacterial protein, aiming at new antibiotics.
This project tests whether abatacept is safe and works for lung disease in people with common variable immune deficiency, and looks at biomarkers of response.
This project offers tools to measure how mitochondria make energy and stay healthy, and how they affect inflammation in aging models.
This project creates a training program on how to move neural medical devices from the lab toward patients, using video lectures and workshops.
This project tests a combination of radiation, dendritic cells and checkpoint inhibitors in patients with a type of bile duct cancer.
This project studies how a protein on B1 cells keeps these cells balanced in atherosclerosis and how its levels relate to coronary artery disease.
This project studies how differences in human genomic diversity shape the way cells commit to their fate and keep their cellular states.
This project studies how genetic variation near a gene tied to telomere length affects cancer risk, aging and other human traits.
This project builds micro and nanofluidic tools to analyze small samples, such as liquid biopsies, for precision medicine.
This project studies a new immune checkpoint pathway in human bladder cancer to understand how it works.
